learn.title: The discriminant
learn.body: The part under the root, $D=b^2-4ac$, is the discriminant. It tells you how many real solutions to expect before you finish: positive means two, zero means one, negative means none.

learn.title: What it means on a graph
learn.body: Solutions are where the parabola meets the $x$-axis. Two solutions: it crosses twice. One: it just touches. None: it floats above or below.

learn.title: A ball in the air
learn.body: Its height is $h=-5t^2+20t$ metres after $t$ seconds.
In a real problem, check whether each solution makes sense. A negative length or time is rejected.

questions.prompt: If $b^2-4ac>0$, how many real solutions are there?
questions.explanation: The root of a positive number gives two different values, plus and minus.
$16-16=0$. So there is exactly one solution, $x=-2$.

questions.prompt: What does that tell you about $x^2+2x+5=0$?
questions.explanation: The root of a negative number is not real, so the parabola never touches the $x$-axis.
The plus and minus versions give the same number, so there is one repeated solution.

questions.prompt: How many real solutions does $x^2-6x+9=0$ have?
For which value of $k$ does $x^2+6x+k=0$ have exactly one solution?
A ball's height is $h=-5t^2+20t$ metres after $t$ seconds. At what time $t>0$ does it land?
questions.explanation: Set $h=0$: $-5t(t-4)=0$, so $t=0$ or $t=4$. It lands at 4 seconds.

questions.prompt: What is the ball's greatest height, in metres?
A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide, and its area is 28 square cm. How wide is it, in cm?
questions.explanation: $w(w+3)=28$, so $w^2+3w-28=0$ and $(w+7)(w-4)=0$. A width cannot be negative, so $w=4$.
